paper.title_en: What determines the properties of Population III binaries?
paper.abstract_en: Population~III binaries may provide a gravitational-wave probe of the first stellar populations. Uncertain initial binary parameter distributions and evolutionary prescriptions complicate predictions of their remnant masses, birth orbits and formation spins. Varying these model evolutionary parameters (MEPs) jointly is needed to identify which MEPs shape each property and whether their effects persist among binaries that merge. We use \textsc{StarTrack} to evolve $2\times10^6$ initial binaries per model across 1152 configurations spanning eight MEPs. To our knowledge, this is the largest grid of Population~III isolated-binary population-synthesis models to date by number of distinct parameter configurations. We compare the properties and correlations of all binary black holes (BBHs) with those of systems that merge within the adopted age of the Universe. The all-BBH (merging-BBH) model medians span $34.3$--$171.0 M_{\odot}$ ($23.1$--$94.8 M_{\odot}$) in total mass, $0.039$--$0.106$ ($0.018$--$0.129$) in effective aligned spin $χ_{\mathrm{eff}}$ at formation, and $0.075$--$0.639$ ($0.039$--$0.983$) in birth eccentricity. Merger selection also changes correlations between BBH properties and the combinations of MEP values and prescriptions associated with them. We use variance-based sensitivity analysis to quantify how the initial binary parameter distributions and evolutionary prescriptions affect the predicted BBH properties.
